_comment: Adapter registry for the arena runner. `cmd` is spawned from the repo root; the corpus is written to its stdin as JSONL and verdicts are read from stdout (see protocol.md). If a cmd can't be spawned (tool not installed, missing API key), the runner marks it unavailable and skips it. Competitor entries are roadmap: their adapter files are not committed yet — see README.md, and note which need an operator-provided API key (cost) versus which are OSS/local-runnable.

adapters.name: warden
adapters.notes: this repo, default posture (no LLM judge)

adapters.name: block-all (paranoid)
adapters.notes: sanity ceiling: 100% recall / 0% precision — proves recall alone is gameable

adapters.name: Meta LlamaFirewall (PromptGuard)
adapters.notes: PARTIAL-AXIS: an LLM-I/O guardrail; PromptGuard screens prompt-injection TEXT, not shell/tool-call actions. Fair only on the injection family (see README threat-model axes). Adapter is committed but UNAVAILABLE until `pip install llamafirewall` + a configured gated Meta HF model — the runner skips it until then. WHY WE DON'T SUBSTITUTE ITS FREE SCANNERS: LlamaFirewall's other scanners do run without a gated model (`CODE_SHIELD` needs only semgrep; `HIDDEN_ASCII` is pure Python, and both are selectable via LLAMAFIREWALL_SCANNERS). But CodeShield detects insecure SOURCE CODE in C/C++/C#/Java/JS/PHP/Python/Rust — it does not support shell — so on a corpus of shell/tool-call actions it would report ALLOW almost everywhere. Publishing a Meta-branded row that scores ~0 because we ran the scanner that was never meant for this input is the strawman this benchmark exists to prevent, so the row stays honestly 'unavailable' instead. WHY WE DON'T USE AN UNGATED MIRROR: third-party re-uploads of Llama-Prompt-Guard-2 exist, but using one to bypass Meta's license gate is circumvention, not benchmarking. Set HF_TOKEN with the license accepted and this row lights up on its real scanner.

adapters.name: LLM Guard (input scanners)
adapters.notes: PARTIAL-AXIS: the guardrail toolkit from Protect AI (now Palo Alto Networks). It screens the TEXT sent to a model, not tool-call semantics, so it is fair on the injection family and is EXPECTED to allow shell RCE — read it as a complementary layer, not a loss (same reading as LlamaFirewall). Scored with the two out-of-box INPUT scanners that need no operator-written rules: PromptInjection (its flagship DeBERTa classifier) and Secrets (detect-secrets, regex/entropy). Code/BanCode are deliberately NOT enabled — this corpus IS commands, so they would flag nearly everything and manufacture a meaningless precision collapse. NO key and NO gated model required: the default `protectai/deberta-v3-base-prompt-injection-v2` is public (only the -small variant is gated), which is why this row runs free in CI. BINARY (valid/invalid) — no human-in-the-loop tier, so it can never earn +gate credit. Needs `pip install llm-guard` and a first-run model download (the Arena workflow installs it and caches the HuggingFace cache).

adapters.name: Pipelock (scan API)
adapters.notes: PARTIAL-AXIS: Pipelock's primary layer is the egress wire (proxy DLP / SSRF / injection scanning); its documented per-call surface is the on-demand Scan API, which is what this adapter drives. Every sample gets every applicable kind (tool_call + dlp on the command string + prompt_injection on skill text), deny from any = block — composition can only raise its recall. Out-of-box posture: no mcp_tool_policy rules (operator-written rules would raise recall on command-semantics families — PRs welcome). Binary allow/deny. Needs a running daemon: `pipelock run --config arena/adapters/pipelock.arena.yaml` (the Arena workflow does this; pinned v3.0.0).

adapters.name: AEGIS (pre-execution check)
adapters.notes: SAME-AXIS: a pre-execution tool-call firewall — the first arena competitor with a genuine THREE-tier verdict. Scored via its documented `POST /api/v1/check` (an open route, no key) in blocking mode, so risky HIGH/CRITICAL calls return `pending` (escalate-to-human) → mapped to gated. Read the +gate column for AEGIS: its hard recall(block) is low BY DESIGN because it escalates rather than hard-blocks. Out-of-box `standard` policy template (shell/supply-chain/prompt-injection→block, file/db→MEDIUM, network→LOW); no operator DSL rules. Fresh agent_id per sample keeps its L2 behavioral-anomaly layer in the 'learning' phase (a stateless corpus can't build a per-agent baseline), so the scored verdict is the deterministic L1-policy + classifier + L3-DSL layer. AEGIS's /check screens the ACTION, not poisoned-skill TEXT, so injection-skill samples that carry no risky argument pass. Needs the gateway on :8080 (the Arena workflow builds + starts it from pinned commit 5f012d5 / v0.2.0). ⚠️ SCORED THROUGH A COMMERCIAL QUOTA — read this before reading its numbers. AEGIS gates POST /api/v1/check behind a Stripe plan quota whose FREE tier is `monthly_checks: 1_000` with `allow_overage: false` (packages/gateway-mcp/src/services/billing.ts); past that it returns 429 to everything. The arena scores each adapter twice per corpus, so a full board run blows through that cap. Unhandled, this produced two FALSE results we nearly published: verdicts differed between the two passes (so the determinism column accused it of declaring a determinism it lacked), and on the 1,212-sample corpus even its startup probe was throttled, so the row silently vanished as 'unavailable'. Neither is a security property — a paywall is not a detection limit. Fix: the workflow restarts the gateway on a fresh database before each corpus (arena/ci/aegis-reset.sh), so every corpus that fits inside 1,000 checks is scored on its merits, and it additionally raises the separate in-memory rate limit (the same allowance made for mcp-firewall). The 1,212-sample tldr corpus does NOT fit even from a clean start, so AEGIS is explicitly EXEMPT there rather than reported as a failing row — we decline to buy a paid plan to benchmark another vendor's tool. Its adapter retries a 429 and then reports an ERROR, so a throttled response is never read as an allow.

adapters.name: mcp-firewall (inbound pipeline)
adapters.notes: SAME-AXIS: an MCP security gateway whose per-call surface is a tool-call firewall. Scored through its own inbound pipeline (kill-switch → rate-limit → injection → egress → policy → chain) in the documented `mcp-firewall init` starter posture, with the global rate-limit disabled (200-call window would deny the last ~45 of 245 on rate alone, not content). THREE-tier: deny→blocked, PROMPT→gated, allow→allowed. We read the RAW stage verdict because its SDK auto-approves prompts to allow on a non-interactive run, which would erase its human-approval tier. ESCALATE-BY-DEFAULT: the starter `defaultAction` is `prompt`, so anything not matched by injection/egress/a rule escalates to a human — expect HIGH +gate recall AND high friction (benign also escalates); read the two together. Injection detector screens prompt-injection TEXT, not shell semantics. Alpha (v0.1.0, no tagged release); pinned by commit 5f01d8b. AGPL-3.0: run as a black box via its SDK, not linked into warden. Needs `pip install git+https://github.com/ressl/mcp-firewall@5f01d8b` (the Arena workflow does this).

roadmap.name: NVIDIA NeMo Guardrails
roadmap.notes: OSS but rail checks are LLM-backed → needs a model endpoint (local or API). Non-deterministic; the determinism-contrast case. Partial-axis (dialog/rail checks, not tool-call classification).

roadmap.name: Claw Patrol (Deno)
roadmap.notes: NOT A LEADERBOARD ROW — different layer. Claw Patrol is a network-wire gateway: it parses protocol traffic (SQL verbs, K8s verb/resource, HTTP path) and gates via HCL rules + credential injection. It does not classify shell/tool-call strings, so this corpus cannot fairly score it. warden + Claw Patrol are complementary layers (the sprayberrylabs 'two layers' write-up), not competitors.

roadmap.name: Lakera Guard
roadmap.notes: cloud API — needs a paid LAKERA_API_KEY. Partial-axis (prompt-injection). Operator decision (key + budget) before wiring.

roadmap.name: Invariant Guardrails (Snyk)
roadmap.notes: SURVEYED, NOT WIRED — and the reason is a fairness rule, not a technical block. `invariant-ai` runs locally with no key (LocalPolicy.from_string(...).analyze(trace)) and is the only surveyed tool that natively matches on ToolCall STRUCTURE, so it is genuinely same-axis. But it is a POLICY ENGINE, not a pretrained classifier: out of the box it ships no rules, so its score would be entirely a function of rules WE write for it. Authoring a competitor's detection logic means authoring its score — in either direction — which no honest scoreboard can do. It belongs here as an invitation: a policy contributed by its own maintainers or users would make a legitimate row. (Also note `extras.py` sets TERMINATE_ON_EXTRA_FAILURE=True — a rule touching prompt_injection/semgrep without extras installed kills the process.)

roadmap.name: Guardrails AI
roadmap.notes: SURVEYED, NOT WIRED. Since 0.11.0 it needs no Hub token (validators ship as plain PyPI dists) and runs LLM-free via Guard().use(...) + guard.validate(text), so cost is not the blocker. The blocker is axis: NONE of its ~65 validators screen shell commands or tool calls. The only rows it could fill are SecretsPresent plus a BanList/RegexMatch denylist we would have to write ourselves — the same author-their-score problem as Invariant. Trap for anyone who tries: 0.11.0 ships contradictory remote-inferencing defaults and its remote endpoint shut down 2026-08-06, so pass use_local=True explicitly and never run `guardrails configure` in CI.

roadmap.name: Vigil
roadmap.notes: EXCLUDED — unmaintained and uninstallable. Never published to PyPI, last push 2024-01-31, requirements pinned to pydantic 1.10.x / numpy 1.25.x which will not build on current Python, and its constructor initializes a vector DB + OpenAI embedder regardless of which scanners are enabled. Listed so nobody re-surveys it.

roadmap.name: mcp-firewall (ressl)
roadmap.notes: OSS MCP security gateway — policy enforcement on tools/call. Same-axis candidate; needs an adapter that drives its policy engine per-call.
